newsitem.title: USA: Texas separatist charged with fraud and conspiracy.
newsitem.headline: Texas separatist charged with fraud and conspiracy.

text.p: The leader of a Texas separatist group was indicted on fraud and conspiracy charges for allegedly issuing $1.8 billion in worthless financial warrants to militia members, federal prosecutors said on Monday.

Republic of Texas "ambassador" Richard McLaren, 43, and his wife Evelyn McLaren, 50, were charged in a 25-count federal indictment with bank fraud, mail fraud and conspiracy for their roles in the scheme, U.S. Attorney Paul Coggins said.

The indictment alleged McLaren issued "Republic of Texas warrants," or bogus financial documents that looked like cashiers checks and were used by militia members to open bank accounts, pay off credit card bills and cover other debts.

"These defendants are not proud Texans but paper terrorists, they are not revolutionaries but rip-off artists, they are not patriots but parasites. In short, they are bullies," Coggins said. "Our message to bullies is: don't mess with Texas."
Five other militia members, whose names were not released, were named as co-conspirators with the McLarens in the grand jury indictment, which was returned under seal last Tuesday, prosecutors said.

The McLarens and four other Republic of Texas members surrendered on Saturday after a standoff with police in the west Texas mountains sparked by the arrest of one of the group's members on state firearms charges.

McLaren and his followers, who claim Texas is an independent nation, had vowed to defend their "embassy" compound to the death but surrendered when scores of police surrounded them and prepared to move in.

Meanwhile, police dogs on Monday were closing in on at least one of two members of the ragtag militia who fled into a canyon in the Davis Mountains hours before the group ended the week-long standoff, a Texas police spokeswoman said.

Five shots were fired and one police bloodhound was injured about an hour after the dogs were set loose and began tracking the men through rugged terrain surrounding the group's compound, spokeswoman Sherri Deatherage Green said.
